content:
“The Topic” being, of course, the Mathocalypse, except sometimes with AI alignment and even quantum computing and complexity theory and other stuff thrown in.

With Ryan Peterman:

Notably, near the end of the above podcast, you can watch my live reaction to the news that an Anthropic model found algorithms for the 3SUM and the All-Pairs-Shortest-Path problems beating records that stood for generations—news that hadn’t yet reached me when I woke up and logged in. (If you don’t feel like watching, my reaction is basically: “uh, wow … if I hadn’t been so overstuffed with delicacies right now from history’s biggest math breakthrough buffet, I’d surely be giving this one the individual amazement that it deserves…”)

And here’s with “Modern CTO”, on a similar set of topics:

Oh, and a third one: MTS podcast with Theo Jaffee.

Enjoy, and thanks to the hosts of these podcasts!

Update (Oct. 19): There’s been a rapid-fire recent sequence of AI-assisted improvements to my 2016 result with Adam Yedidia, showing that the 8000th Busy Beaver number eludes the axioms of set theory. I haven’t even kept track of all of them, but the very latest, by friend-of-the-blog Elliot Glazer, shows that the value of BB(230) is independent of ZFC (see here for explanation).
